title: Zuriel Bible Geography Atlas — Study Foundation
description: Original geography study metadata for biblical places and journeys. Coordinates and route polylines are intentionally omitted until independently verified; modern borders are not ancient borders.
editorialPolicy: References identify passages to read; they are not substitutes for the full text.
Ancient place identifications can be debated. Uncertain identifications are labelled rather than presented as settled facts.
Modern country labels are present-day orientation only and must not be projected onto biblical political boundaries.
No generated coordinates, archaeological claims, copyrighted map tiles or Bible text are included.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.significance: The city associated with David's kingship, the temple, Jesus' final week, crucifixion and resurrection proclamation.
places.studyCaution: Distinguish the historical city, its temple precincts and later theological uses of Zion.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.significance: David's town and the birthplace of Jesus in Matthew and Luke.
places.studyCaution: Micah's prophecy and Gospel fulfilment should be read in their literary contexts.

places.name: Nazareth
places.significance: The town where Jesus grew up and where Luke records his synagogue reading.
places.studyCaution: Do not confuse Jesus' upbringing in Nazareth with the location of his birth.

places.name: Capernaum
places.region: Northwest shore of Sea of Galilee
places.significance: A major setting for Jesus' Galilean ministry, teaching and healings.
places.studyCaution: Gospel accounts describe multiple events in this town; avoid assuming every Galilee event occurred here.

places.name: Sea of Galilee
places.significance: Freshwater lake central to Jesus' calling of disciples, teaching, crossings and signs.
places.studyCaution: Also called the Sea of Tiberias or Lake of Gennesaret in the New Testament.

places.name: Jordan River
places.significance: A major river in Israel's story, including crossing narratives and John's baptism ministry.
places.studyCaution: Several biblical events occur at different stretches; do not assign an exact modern baptism site without evidence.

places.name: Jericho
places.significance: An ancient city in the conquest narrative and the setting of Jesus' encounter with Zacchaeus.
places.studyCaution: Joshua's account and the Gospel-era city belong to different historical periods.

places.name: Bethany
places.region: East of Jerusalem, near Mount of Olives
places.significance: Associated with Mary, Martha and Lazarus, and with events near Jesus' final days.
places.studyCaution: Keep Bethany distinct from Bethabara/Bethany beyond the Jordan in John 1:28 textual traditions.

places.name: Mount of Olives
places.significance: A ridge linked with Jesus' teaching, prayer and departure/return imagery.
places.studyCaution: Prophetic texts use the mountain symbolically as well as geographically.

places.name: Gethsemane
places.significance: The garden or olive grove where Jesus prayed before his arrest.
places.studyCaution: The Gospels identify the place by name; exact archaeological boundaries are not certain.

places.name: Samaria
places.significance: A region with a complex history of Israelite and Samaritan communities; Jesus' ministry crosses its boundaries.
places.studyCaution: Avoid treating all Samaritans as identical or reducing the region to a single town.

places.name: Sychar
places.significance: The setting near Jacob's well where Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman.
places.studyCaution: The precise identification of Sychar remains debated; distinguish it from Shechem.

places.name: Caesarea Maritima
places.significance: A Roman administrative centre associated with Philip, Peter, Paul and Roman governors.
places.studyCaution: Do not confuse Caesarea Maritima with Caesarea Philippi.

places.name: Caesarea Philippi
places.significance: The setting of Peter's confession in the Synoptic Gospel tradition.
places.studyCaution: A different city from Caesarea Maritima on the coast.

places.name: Tyre and Sidon
places.significance: Coastal cities appearing in prophetic texts and in accounts of Jesus' ministry beyond Galilee.
places.studyCaution: Ancient city names cover long-lived settlements; modern borders differ from ancient political geography.

places.name: Damascus
places.significance: A major ancient city and the setting of Saul's encounter with the risen Jesus.
places.studyCaution: The conversion narrative is recounted in Acts more than once with differing narrative emphases.

places.name: Antioch (Syria)
places.significance: A key early Christian centre where disciples were first called Christians and from which missions were sent.
places.studyCaution: Distinguish Syrian Antioch from Pisidian Antioch in Acts 13.

places.name: Pisidian Antioch
places.significance: A city visited by Paul and Barnabas during the first missionary journey.
places.studyCaution: Not the same place as Antioch on the Orontes.

places.name: Ephesus
places.significance: A major setting for Paul's teaching, the Ephesian church and the ministry of the word in Acts.
places.studyCaution: The letter to the Ephesians is addressed to a Christian audience; debates about its destination should be noted in advanced study.

places.name: Philippi
places.significance: The setting of Lydia's conversion, the jailer's household and Paul's early European mission.
places.studyCaution: Acts' travel narrative places Philippi within Paul's Macedonian mission.

places.name: Thessalonica
places.significance: A city where Paul preached and a church received letters addressing faith, hope and endurance.
places.studyCaution: Separate the city's history from later church tradition.

places.name: Athens
places.significance: The setting of Paul's address at the Areopagus, engaging local religious and philosophical ideas.
places.studyCaution: Acts presents Paul's speech as contextual proclamation, not endorsement of every Athenian belief.

places.name: Corinth
places.significance: A major port city where Paul ministered and wrote to address church unity, holiness and resurrection hope.
places.studyCaution: The two New Testament letters address distinct situations and should not be flattened into one occasion.

places.name: Rome
places.significance: The imperial capital and destination of Paul's journey in Acts; the setting for the letter to the Romans.
places.studyCaution: Acts ends with Paul under house arrest; it does not narrate his later death.

places.name: Patmos
places.significance: The island where John says he received the Revelation while in exile or confinement because of God's word and testimony.
places.studyCaution: The text identifies the island but does not provide a detailed itinerary of John's life.

journeys.name: Abraham's migration
journeys.studyCaution: A broad migration sequence; the exact route and identification of Ur are discussed by historians.

journeys.name: Exodus and wilderness journey
journeys.sequence: Egypt → Sea crossing → Sinai → wilderness → plains of Moab
journeys.studyCaution: The biblical itinerary names stages, but some modern site identifications remain disputed.

journeys.name: Conquest crossing
journeys.studyCaution: Read the narrative's theological framing alongside archaeological and historical discussions.

journeys.name: Jesus' Galilean ministry
journeys.sequence: Nazareth ↔ Capernaum ↔ towns around the Sea of Galilee
journeys.studyCaution: A regional ministry overview, not a precise day-by-day travel map.

journeys.name: Journey to Jerusalem
journeys.studyCaution: Luke's travel section is a literary journey narrative as well as a geographical movement.

journeys.name: Paul's first missionary journey
journeys.sequence: Antioch (Syria) → Cyprus → Pisidian Antioch → Iconium → Lystra → Derbe → return
journeys.studyCaution: The sequence follows Acts; route lines should be illustrative rather than precise road reconstructions.

journeys.name: Paul's second missionary journey
journeys.sequence: Antioch (Syria) → Asia Minor → Troas → Philippi → Thessalonica → Athens → Corinth
journeys.studyCaution: Acts records changes in plans and Spirit-led direction; not every leg has a securely identified road.

journeys.name: Paul's journey to Rome
journeys.sequence: Caesarea → sea voyage → Malta → Syracuse → Rhegium → Puteoli → Rome
journeys.studyCaution: The storm and shipwreck account gives named stages; exact ship track is not fully recoverable.
